title: Confederation Park plan and Fergus-area bridge decisions
subtitle: Development charges public meeting, water-system grant agreement, heritage designations and a provincial road resurfacing announcement
overview: Council endorsed the Confederation Park Revitalization Plan {{vote:m2}}, a phased guide for accessibility, safety and invasive species removal in the Fergus park. Phase one work can begin within the $150,000 already budgeted, with staff looking to community partners and grants for the remainder.

Council also endorsed replacing Bridges 21-WG and 29-WG and removing Bridge 30-WG without replacement {{vote:m3}}. Staff will publish the Notice of Study Completion. Council approved a by-law to sign the provincial Housing Enabling Water Systems Fund agreement {{vote:m4}}, which staff said provides about $6.8 million toward servicing the South Fergus secondary plan area. Consent items, approved together {{vote:m1}}, included intentions to designate three properties under the Ontario Heritage Act, and by-laws making those designations passed {{vote:m5}}.

Before the regular meeting, council held a public meeting on the proposed development charges background study and by-law. No decision was made. Home builders and developers asked for more time and lower increases. Council is expected to consider the by-law on March 23. The MPP announced Connecting Links funding for road resurfacing in Fergus, and the mayor reported the County budget, adopted with a 3.6% increase.

decisions.detail: Council received the report and endorsed the plan's recommendations, a phased approach to accessibility, safety and stewardship, with phase one to start within the $150,000 budget.
Council endorsed Alternative No. 8, replacing Bridges 21-WG and 29-WG and removing Bridge 30-WG without replacement, and directed staff to publish the Notice of Study Completion.

decisions.item: Housing Enabling Water Systems Fund agreement
decisions.detail: Council authorized the CAO and the Managing Director of Corporate Services/Treasurer to sign the Ontario Transfer Payment Agreement for Intake 2 of the fund.

decisions.item: Consent items including heritage designation intentions
decisions.detail: Council approved the consent items, which included confirming intent to designate 179 Victoria Crescent and 64 Colborne Street in Elora and 7324 Wellington Road 21 in Pilkington as heritage properties.
Council passed By-laws 2026-11 to 2026-14, authorizing the water systems agreement and designating the three properties under the Ontario Heritage Act.

debate: At the development charges public meeting, builder-industry delegates said the proposed increases come at a poor time for housing starts and affordability. They argued the costs flow through to buyers and asked council to defer adoption for more review time. Council did not act at this meeting.

Developer delegates raised concern about treatment of urban boundary expansion lands, warning of a two-tier system, and asked that some servicing projects be moved earlier to match planned housing. The consultant said the addendum removed the original local service approach for such expansions but kept a requirement for developers to fund study updates in some cases.

Councillors asked whether charges could be phased in, why apartment rates rise more than single-detached rates, and how deferral and affordable housing exemptions work. The consultant said phasing is council's choice but the discounted amount must be funded from taxes or rates, and that rates follow per-person calculations required by the Act.

On Confederation Park, one councillor cautioned that invasive species removal needs native replanting and that trimming near the lookout could affect shade and the river. The consultants said replacement planning is budgeted and sightline work means limb trimming. Another councillor raised low-head dam safety, portage access and lighting, which staff said would be addressed in detailed design.

On Bridge 30-WG, one councillor spoke of the farming community's reliance on Side Road 15 and asked for further consideration. Another noted public comments mostly favoured removal and raised intersection safety concerns. The consultant said the bridge scored lower on environmental and cost criteria, and that most weighting scenarios still favoured the recommended option.
